title: v2 bot signature binds URL pathname only; GET query string (status/search/sort/page/limit) is unsigned
claim: The v2 HMAC canonical path is `new URL(https://internal${path}).pathname`, so the query string that getPresets builds (status, search, sort, page, limit) is outside the signature; presets-api verifies against the same pathname (apps/presets-api/src/middleware/auth.ts:315), so both sides agree. No reachable attacker today: the request travels only over the PRESETS_API service binding, so this only matters if a query parameter ever becomes authorization-relevant or the URL fallback is used outside dev.
evidence: preset-api.ts:120 `path: new URL(`https://internal${path}`).pathname,`; preset-api.ts:228-229 `return request<PresetListResponse>(env, 'GET', `/api/v1/presets${query ? `?${query}` : ''}`);`; packages/auth/src/hmac.ts:280-291 canonicalV2 fields = v2, method, path, sha256(body), timestamp, nonce, userDiscordId, userName (no query).

title: Message-component interactions bypass the per-user rate limiter

title: /glamour has no tier of its own and spends one shared api-worker service key
claim: /glamour has no entry in DISCORD_COMMAND_LIMITS, so it falls to the default of 15/min per user. Every run spends one request against api-worker's single shared service key, SERVICE_LIMIT 1300/60 s with SERVICE_KEY 'workers'. About 87 Discord accounts per colo can fill that key, after which every user's /glamour answers RESOLVE_BUSY. Varied gear numbers also make each call a cache-missing XIVAPI search. Impact is bounded: the public /v1/chara/resolve already allows 60/min per IP, so this is a cross-user availability lever on the bot path, not a new amplifier.

On a 429 the bot replies busy: packages/bot-logic/src/commands/glamour.ts:469-471. One resolve per run: apps/discord-worker/src/handlers/commands/glamour.ts:54-98.

title: POST /presets spends a Perspective call before reserving quota; a same-dye concurrent burst is charged one submission
claim: POST /presets only runs a read-only daily-cap pre-check (presets.ts:998), then calls moderateContent/Perspective (:1031). A dye_signature UNIQUE collision then returns through respondToDuplicate (:1058-1064, :171-205) without writing a submission_events row, so N concurrent POSTs with one fresh dye set make N Perspective calls but are charged one submission. Repeating this with a new dye set for each of the 10 daily submissions lets one account drive Perspective (~1 QPS quota) to 429, which pushes other users' concurrent submissions and edits into perspective_unavailable -> pending. It fails closed, so nothing gets published, but auto-approval and the moderator queue are degraded. PATCH avoids this by reserving before the call (presets.ts:683). Inferred from code; not raced live.
evidence: presets.ts:998 `const rateLimitResult = await checkSubmissionRateLimit(...)` (no reservation); :1031 `const moderationResult = await moderateContent(body.name, body.description, c.env, ...)`; :1058 `if (isDyeSignatureCollision(error)) { ... return respondToDuplicate(c, auth, existingPreset); }`; :1075 `await recordSubmissionEvent(..., 'submission', preset.id, ...)` only after a successful createPreset. Compare :683 `reserveDailyEvent(c.env.DB, auth.userDiscordId, 'text_edit', ...)` before moderateContent on PATCH.

The owner of any preset can keep posting up to 5 MB bodies that pass the magic-byte sniff but fail in photon, limited only by the 100/min per-user limiter. 'Image could not be processed' }, 400); }`; rate-limit-service.ts:320-322 release = `DELETE FROM submission_events WHERE id = ?`; preview-image-service.ts:143-153 throws on !response.ok after `IMAGE_WORKER.fetch(... signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000))`.

title: Per-IP /auth/* limiter keys on the full IPv6 address, so one /64 gets an unlimited number of independent buckets
claim: getClientIp returns CF-Connecting-IP lowercased with no IPv6 prefix aggregation, and oauth keys the native RL_AUTH_* binding on `${ip}:${path}`. A client with a routed IPv6 /64 can rotate source addresses and get a fresh 10/20/30-per-minute budget per address, so the token-exchange and login-initiation limits do not bound one client (this amplifies upstream Discord/XIVAuth token calls; there is no credential to brute force because state + PKCE bind each exchange). Precondition not confirmable from the repo: IPv6 enabled on the auth.xivdyetools.app zone (Cloudflare default). The helper is shared, so every worker using getClientIp has the same property.
evidence: packages/worker-kit/src/rate-limiter/ip.ts:61-63 `const cfIp = request.headers.get('CF-Connecting-IP'); if (cfIp) { return normalizeIp(cfIp.trim()); }` and :87-89 `function normalizeIp(ip) { return ip.toLowerCase(); }`; apps/oauth/src/services/rate-limit.ts:145 `const key = `${ip}:${path}`;`; worker-kit backends/cloudflare.ts:181 `const bindingKey = `${this.keyPrefix}${key}:t${tier.limit}_${tier.periodSeconds}`;` (no masking). `git grep -n -i ipv6 -- packages/worker-kit/src` shows no /64 handling.

title: OAuth state is HMAC'd with the JWT signing key: an unauthenticated signing oracle under JWT_SECRET with no domain separation
claim: GET /auth/discord and /auth/xivauth return HMAC-SHA256(JWT_SECRET, base64url(JSON)) over a JSON whose csrf, code_challenge and return_path the caller chooses, using the same key and primitive that sign JWTs. Not exploitable today because a JWT signing input always contains '.' and a state's never does, and the only other JWT_SECRET consumer is presets-api's JWT verify; it is a latent cross-protocol risk if any future HMAC(JWT_SECRET) use signs dot-free data.
evidence: state-signing.ts:35-40 `const encodedState = base64UrlEncode(json); const signature = await signJwtData(encodedState, secret);`; oauth-flow.ts:190-203 builds stateData from caller `state`, `code_challenge`, `return_path` and calls `signState(stateData, c.env.JWT_SECRET)`; jwt-service.ts:83-84 `const signatureInput = `${encodedHeader}.${encodedPayload}`; const signature = await signJwtData(signatureInput, secret);`. `git grep -n JWT_SECRET -- 'apps/*/src/**/*.ts'` outside oauth: only presets-api/src/middleware/auth.ts:100 (sharedVerifyJWT).

title: No cache-miss upstream budget on /v1/chara/*; new icon ?version= gives a per-request cache bypass
claim: A client can choose cache-cold keys on every request: the resolve key includes the variant lane, and the new icon ?version= accepts any canonical 16-hex value as cacheable without checking it. Each request then becomes one XIVAPI search or asset fetch under the project's fixed User-Agent, plus up to 12 eight-day empty-family cache writes. The only throttle is the shared 65/60 s per-IP API bucket, which fails open and has no miss-only limiter like Universalis (FINDING-011) and no backoff on an upstream 429. Unconfirmed precondition: how XIVAPI answers an unknown version key. A 400 or 404 means nothing is cached, but the upstream call is still made.
evidence: xivapi.ts:294-296 `const version = versionOverride ?? this.version; if (isCanonicalVersion(version)) return { base: this.base, version, cacheable: true };` | router.ts:306-314 accepts any `^[0-9a-f]{16}$` version | icon-cache.ts:28 key = [policy, base, version, iconId] | core chara-models.ts:80-92 key packs variant | lookup-loader.ts:61-62 stores every miss | rate-limit.ts:31 `failOpen: true` 65/min | xivapi.ts:399-400 throws on 429, no backoff | commit 4b03e9e8 (after 2026-10-03) added version. Prior note: the 2026-10-03 evidence review-api-worker-chara-universalis-telemetry.md:57 left the resolve-side cache pollution unfiled (evidence only, not in the report's Rejected list).

title: XIVAPI search and Glasses bodies are read with an unbounded response.json()
claim: searchItems and getGlasses buffer the whole upstream body with response.json(). Other upstream reads in the worker are byte-capped: the context probe at 32 KiB, icons at 1 MiB, Universalis at 5 MB. Any client can trigger the call, but harm needs XIVAPI or the var-configured base to send an oversized body. This was routed as a robustness handoff on 2026-10-03 and is still unfixed.

title: Invalid world/DC names cause uncharged upstream list fetches
claim: When a datacenter/world name misses the static allowlist, the handler awaits two cachedFetch calls (/data-centers and /worlds) with no onMiss hook, so they are never charged to the per-IP limiter (the charge exists only on the aggregated fetch at router.ts:215). While those caches are cold or Universalis is failing, every request with a random name makes two upstream fetches, because failures are not negatively cached and coalescing is per-isolate only.
evidence: if (!isValidDatacenterOrWorld(datacenter)) { ... Promise.all([cachedFetch({cacheKey:'data-centers:all',...}), cachedFetch({cacheKey:'worlds:all',...})]) } // no onMiss: chargeLimiter. Precondition: cold cache or upstream error; with warm 24h cache cost is nil.

title: 16-bit PNG within the pixel cap overruns the isolate memory limit (pixel budget assumes 4 B/px)
claim: MAX_PIXEL_COUNT is derived assuming 4 bytes per decoded pixel and 2 copies, but a 16-bit RGBA PNG decodes at roughly 15.6 bytes/px of wasm memory, so a tiny (73 KB) 3072x3072 16-bit PNG that passes the header gate drives wasm linear memory to ~147 MB, above the 128 MB isolate limit. A Discord user (via /extract, cdn.discordapp.com URL) or an authenticated preset author (via presets-api /thumbnail) can therefore kill the image-worker isolate and fail concurrent requests; precondition: the Node measurement carries over to workerd, which I could not run.
evidence: Probe in scratchpad with real @cf-wasm/photon (WebAssembly.Instance memory hooked): 3072x3072 RGBA PNG, header gate readImageDimensions -> {3072,3072} (=MAX_PIXEL_COUNT 9437184, passes validateDimensions validators.ts:281-283). new_from_byteslice: depth 8 -> wasm memory 110.25 MB; depth 16 -> 146.875 MB (file 73,452 B). The 8-bit peak alone already sits near 110 MB, so the 'peak near 95-100 MB' margin in validators.ts:74-80 is thin. dimensions.ts readPng (line ~46) ignores bit depth; no bit-depth/color-type check anywhere.

title: Logger: a non-Error `error` argument skips key-name redaction (cookie, session_id, webhook_url, nested keys)
claim: `formatError` passes any non-Error value through `safeStringify` and then only through the free-text `SANITIZE_RULES`. The key-name list and the `SENSITIVE_SUFFIX` check never run on it, so keys such as `cookie`, `session_id`, `webhook_url`, `set_cookie` and their nested copies are emitted verbatim. The same object passed as context is redacted. Five in-repo call sites already pass a context-shaped object as the error argument (discord-worker index.ts:319, :916; moderation-worker index.ts:239; presets-api retention-job.ts:86; stoat-worker index.ts:70). Their values are harmless today, so this is a misuse trap rather than a live leak, and Workers Logs are off in production.
evidence: base-logger.ts:268-273: `const raw = typeof error === 'string' ? error : safeStringify(error); return { name: 'Unknown', message: this.config.sanitizeErrors ? this.sanitizeErrorMessage(raw) : raw };`. Probe scratchpad/probe-err.ts, `log.error('obj', {cookie:'sid=abc', session_id:'s1', webhook_url:'https://x/y', nested:{cookie:'c2'}})`, emitted `"cookie":"sid=abc","session_id":"s1","webhook_url":"https://x/y" ... "nested":{"cookie":"c2"}`. The same object passed as context gave `cookie:[REDACTED], session_id:[REDACTED]`. Signature at logger types.ts:111: `error(message: string, error?: unknown, context?: LogContext)`.

title: Logger value-shape redaction misses Discord webhook / interaction-token URLs
claim: `SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS` covers Bearer, JWT, Discord bot tokens and 64+ hex runs, but not `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/<id>/<token>`. A webhook URL or interaction follow-up URL under an innocuous key (`url`, `followup`) or in message text is logged intact. discord-worker builds these URLs (utils/discord-api.ts:76, :165, :340) but was not seen logging them, and moderation-worker strips them with its own `sanitizeUrl`, so no path is confirmed.

title: JWT and V2 bot signatures accept non-canonical encodings (signature malleability)
claim: `base64UrlDecodeBytes` maps `-`/`_`, pads and calls the forgiving `atob`, which also accepts `+`/`/`, ASCII whitespace, explicit `=` padding and non-zero trailing bits. As a result, several different token strings verify for one HMAC. `hexToBytes` accepts upper-case hex, so the same holds for V2 bot signatures. No consumer keys a cache or blacklist on the raw token string (revocation keys by `jti`, and the bot nonce cache keys by nonce), so no bypass was found.
evidence: Probe scratchpad/probe-jwt.mts: the `trailingBits`, `stdAlphabet`, `whitespace` and `padded` variants each print `true true` (string differs from the original, verifyJWT accepts it), and `v2 upper hex true`. Code at base64.ts:256-265: `let base64 = str.replace(/-/g,'+').replace(/_/g,'/'); ... const binary = atob(base64);` and jwt.ts:160 `base64UrlDecodeBytes(signatureB64)`. Grep for `.get|put|set|has(...token...)` in the oauth, presets-api and api-worker src directories found no matches.

title: getClientIp JSDoc says X-Forwarded-For is trusted by default; the code defaults to false
claim: The usage example and an inline comment both describe `trustXForwardedFor` as defaulting to true, but the code defaults it to false. A consumer who follows the published docs may misjudge which header keys the rate limiter, either opting in to spoofable XFF or assuming it is already honoured. No in-repo consumer opts in.

title: GPOSERS text() regex is quadratic on long non-newline whitespace runs
claim: The regex /\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g in text() takes quadratic time on a long run of whitespace that contains no newline. It is applied to item names, dye names and Acquisition lines by gposersGroups, which bot-logic /glamour (glamour.ts:405-409, Worker CPU) and the web export sheet call. The inputs come from XIVAPI names relayed by api-worker and from the web user's own uncapped textarea (glamour-sheet.ts:266-284, self-only). An attacker would need to control the upstream XIVAPI answer, which I could not confirm is possible.
evidence: node: s='a'+' '.repeat(n)+'b'; s.replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g,' ') took 63.9ms at n=8192 and 4162.8ms at n=65536. Source: `return value?.replace(/\s*[\r\n]+\s*/g, ' ').trim() ?? '';` (chara-gposers.ts:120).

title: Legacy parseCharaFile is still a published export without the facade's bounds and echoes input in errors
claim: parseCharaFile is still exported from the core barrel. It uses native JSON.parse with no byte cap, no depth limit, and last-wins duplicate keys, and its AppError messages quote up to 64 characters of file input. No in-repo production code calls it (web and bot use inspectCharaForTools), so only an external npm consumer that passes it untrusted text is exposed.

Tribe 'constructor' produced `.chara field Tribe: unrecognised value "constructor" (expected one of: ...)` (chara-parser.ts:340-347, describeValue at 233-245).

title: sanitizeEmbedText does not strip bidi isolates, Arabic letter mark or tag characters
claim: The INVISIBLE class covers U+200B-200F, U+202A-202E and U+2060-2064 but omits the bidi isolates U+2066-2069, U+061C and the tag block U+E0000-E007F, although the docblock promises that bidi controls are stripped. A user-controlled preset name, description or author name can therefore reorder or hide text in a bot-authored embed.
evidence: Probe with the same regex: input 'a⁦b⁧c⁩d؜e\u{E0041}' came back unchanged in length 11 after replace(INVISIBLE,''). Source lines 22-26 list only the ranges above; line 63 applies it in sanitizeEmbedText.

title: escapeDiscordMarkdown leaves Discord angle-bracket syntax live
claim: MARKDOWN_SPECIALS escapes '>' but not '<', and defuseMentions only handles <@..>, so user text such as <#channelId>, </command:id>, <id:customize>, <:emoji:id> or <t:...> still renders as a channel link, slash-command mention, guild navigation link, emoji or timestamp inside bot-voiced embeds. No ping occurs because allowed_mentions is none, and a slash mention only prefills a command for the clicker, so the effect is bounded spoofing.
evidence: Line 14: const MARKDOWN_SPECIALS = /([*_~`|>#\\[\]()])/g (no '<'); lines 47-51 defuseMentions replaces only /@(everyone|here)/ and /<@[!&]?(\d+)>/.

title: Beta bot deployed from any unreviewed branch can hold production's moderator-equivalent presets-api signing pair
claim: presets-api has a single BOT_API_SECRET/BOT_SIGNING_SECRET pair, and any holder can sign any X-User-Discord-ID; it is granted isModerator for every id in MODERATOR_IDS (apps/presets-api/src/middleware/auth.ts:339-345, src/types.ts:136-137). title: Upstream XIVAuth email auto-merge links a new provider identity to an existing account and signs in with no owner confirmation or MFA; via oauth this yields a presets-api JWT carrying the victim's discord_id
deploy_unit: gap (upstream XIVAuth a4e6693; impact lands in oauth + presets-api)
claim: When no (provider, uid) identity exists, XIVAuth looks up any user by the provider-reported email, attaches the incoming identity to that user and signs in via sso_signin (:60-62). The MFA step exists only in sessions_controller.rb:136-150, so this skips it. Anyone holding a provider account whose 'verified' email equals a victim's XIVAuth email gets the victim's XIVAuth session. oauth then resolves the victim's row by xivauth_id (user-service.ts:73-77) and mints the victim's discord_id (jwt-service.ts:141). In presets-api that allows edit and delete (presets.ts:437,587), voting, and moderator rights if the victim is a moderator (auth.ts:365). Precondition: the attacker must control a mailbox at a provider that verifies email, or a provider that returns unverified emails. Discord gates on verified (lib/omniauth/discord.rb:23). The GitHub and Twitch gems are not vendored, so their gating is unconfirmed. This is upstream's to fix and should be reported separately; on our side it could only be narrowed.
evidence:
omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb:109-116:
  email = auth.dig(:info, :email)
  return nil if email.blank?
  existing_user = User.find_for_database_authentication(email: email.downcase)
  existing_user&.add_social_identity(auth)
  existing_user
and :60-62 `sign_in_and_redirect @user` with no MFA prompt. Upstream tip confirmed with `git ls-remote origin HEAD` = a4e669343add.

title: oauth never clears or re-checks a row's Discord link, so a Discord id once attached stays the presets-api identity after XIVAuth stops asserting it
claim: attachIdentities only fills an empty discord_id and keeps existing.discord_id in every other case. A null linkedDiscordId from xivauth.ts:346 is ignored, and no route unlinks or deletes an account. Once an XIVAuth account's row holds snowflake D, that account keeps minting discord_id=D even after D is unlinked upstream (social_identities_controller.rb:4-10). D's real owner who signs in with Discord lands on the same row (findOrCreateUser step 2, user-service.ts:81-86) and cannot evict the stale xivauth_id. That only changes when a different XIVAuth account asserting D signs in (:202-208). This turns a one-time upstream mis-link (candidate 01) into permanent impersonation. With a legitimate link there is no effect.

title: presets-api never enforces the author ban on moderator approve/revert; the only guard is moderation-worker's non-atomic pre-check

title: Owner can keep moderator reject/revert permanently STALE_REVIEW with uncapped tag/category/link edits
claim: The content_revision trigger also fires on tags, category_id, secondary_categories, example_link and author_name. An owner edit that changes only those charges no daily slot (the text_edit reservation sits inside if(textChanged)) and leaves an approved preset approved, so it is capped only by the 100/min per-user limiter. Moderator /status and /revert are bound to the reviewed revision, and the reject flow is a human confirm, modal and typed-reason loop. An author looping tag edits about once a second therefore makes every reject return 409 STALE_REVIEW and keeps an offensive approved preset public. Ban (a direct D1 hide that is not revision-bound) and moderator DELETE still work, which bounds the impact.

title: .chara Nickname/TypeName projection can be ill-formed UTF-16 (lone or split surrogates)

title: /glamour embed truncation math fails when the notes tail exceeds the budget; the failed edit is silent
claim: If tail.length > ~3996, body.lastIndexOf('\n', EMBED_BUDGET - tail.length - 4) gets a negative position and returns -1, so body.slice(0,-1) keeps almost the whole body.
